From 08b096c1372cd69627f4f559fb47c9fb67a52b39 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Qu Wenruo <wqu@suse.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Jan 2026 20:26:40 +1030
Subject: [PATCH] btrfs: send: check for inline extents in
 range_is_hole_in_parent()

Before accessing the disk_bytenr field of a file extent item we need
to check if we are dealing with an inline extent.
This is because for inline extents their data starts at the offset of
the disk_bytenr field. So accessing the disk_bytenr
means we are accessing inline data or in case the inline data is less
than 8 bytes we can actually cause an invalid
memory access if this inline extent item is the first item in the leaf
or access metadata from other items.

Fixes: 82bfb2e7b645 ("Btrfs: incremental send, fix unnecessary hole writes for sparse files")
Reviewed-by: Filipe Manana <fdmanana@suse.com>
Signed-off-by: Qu Wenruo <wqu@suse.com>
Reviewed-by: David Sterba <dsterba@suse.com>
Signed-off-by: David Sterba <dsterba@suse.com>

diff --git a/fs/btrfs/send.c b/fs/btrfs/send.c
index 130aabced207..d0b2f9bd4150 100644
--- a/fs/btrfs/send.c
+++ b/fs/btrfs/send.c
@@ -6382,6 +6382,8 @@ static int range_is_hole_in_parent(struct send_ctx *sctx,
 		extent_end = btrfs_file_extent_end(path);
 		if (extent_end <= start)
 			goto next;
+		if (btrfs_file_extent_type(leaf, fi) == BTRFS_FILE_EXTENT_INLINE)
+			return 0;
 		if (btrfs_file_extent_disk_bytenr(leaf, fi) == 0) {
 			search_start = extent_end;
 			goto next;
-- 
2.34.1

### Summary of Modifications

The patch addresses a bug in the Btrfs send mechanism by adding a safety check for inline file extent items in the function `range_is_hole_in_parent()`. Previously, the function accessed the `disk_bytenr` field of a file extent item without first verifying whether the extent was inline. For inline extents, the `disk_bytenr` field does not contain a disk address; instead it marks the start of inline data. Accessing it could lead to reading invalid memory or interpreting inline data as a disk address, potentially causing crashes or incorrect behavior.

#### Changes per File

- **`fs/btrfs/send.c`**: Added a condition in `range_is_hole_in_parent()` to check if the file extent type is `BTRFS_FILE_EXTENT_INLINE`. If it is, the function now returns `0` immediately (indicating no hole) instead of proceeding to read the `disk_bytenr`. This prevents any further processing of the inline extent’s `disk_bytenr` field.

#### Relationship Between Modifications

There is only one modification in a single file. The added check is placed before the existing check that reads `disk_bytenr`, ensuring that inline extents are excluded from subsequent logic that could cause the vulnerability. This fix directly addresses the root cause described in the commit message: unsafe access to inline extent data.
